hints: Look closely at the two sugar shapes (pentagons) and the P circles in each diagram. In real DNA the two strands run in opposite directions, so the sugars should be flipped relative to each other.
Now check the middle of each pair. Remember A always pairs with T using 2 hydrogen bonds, and C always pairs with G using 3 hydrogen bonds. Count the dashed lines.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two rules for a DNA base pair**

Think like a checker. First, the bases must be a correct pair. Second, the backbones must be antiparallel.

Correct pairs and bonds:
$$A-T = 2 \text{ hydrogen bonds, } C-G = 3 \text{ hydrogen bonds}$$

**Check antiparallel orientation**

Look at the pentagons (deoxyribose) and P (phosphate). In A and B one sugar points up and the other points down, so the strands are antiparallel. That is correct.

In C and D both sugars point the same way with both P circles on the same side, so the strands are parallel. That is wrong for DNA.

**Check hydrogen bond number**

Now look at the dashed lines in the middle. Diagram A shows an A-T pair but with 3 dashed lines. A-T should have only 2, so A is out.

Diagram B shows a C-G pair with 3 dashed lines. That matches perfectly, plus it is antiparallel. So B is the winner.

options.A: Shows correct A-T pairing and antiparallel sugars, but shows 3 hydrogen bonds instead of 2 for A-T.
options.B: Shows correct C-G pairing with 3 hydrogen bonds and the two sugars in opposite (antiparallel) orientation.
options.C: Shows correct C-G pairing with 3 bonds, but both sugars face the same way so the strands are parallel, not antiparallel.
options.D: Shows correct A-T pairing, but both sugars face the same way so the strands are parallel, not antiparallel.
